context.body: David wants to build a house for God; the word through Nathan reverses the direction and promises David a house, offspring, kingdom, father-son relationship, and enduring throne.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The chapter does not use the noun covenant, but later Scripture explicitly remembers this promise as covenant with David.
observations.label: House, son, throne, forever: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David builds? → God will build David a house visible within its covenant claim.
observations.label: House, son, throne, forever: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David · offspring · House · throne · Kingdom · sonship · enduring throne · David builds? → God will build David a house
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 7:8–17

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 7:8–17 as its own david covenant setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places David builds? → God will build David a house inside this covenant setting without turning it into a definition for every covenant passage.
